Subject: Intermittent hosted inference degradation (US-West) — status & follow-up

Hi Elena / James / Ops team,

Short update: we are currently observing degraded performance (increased latency and a small spike in 5xx) for hosted inference traffic originating from the US‑West region. The issue began at ~08:45 UTC (00:45 PT) and affects text-generation endpoints only — embeddings are unaffected.

What we're seeing:
- 95th percentile generation latency increased from ~180ms to ~1.2s for a subset of requests.
- ~1.8% of calls returned 5xx between 08:45–08:55 UTC.

Immediate actions taken:
- We activated routing fallbacks to smaller compatible model variants for customer-facing routes.
- Engineers rolled a targeted restart of a misbehaving serving pool in us-west-2.
- Auto-scaling thresholds were temporarily adjusted to favor additional concurrency.

Current impact: many requests are back to normal after the restart and routing change, but we are still monitoring and throttling some jobs to prevent recurrence. We expect to reach a stable state within the next ~45–60 minutes.

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-0412-1
Action for you: please validate if your critical endpoints are behaving normally and share any request ids that still return errors. It helps our triage.

We will follow up with a detailed postmortem and remediation plan once we finish root-cause analysis.

Apologies for the disruption — I know this is disruptive for Horizon Health’s clinical ingest pipelines. We’ll keep you posted.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Intermittent hosted inference degradation (US-West) — status & follow-up

Thanks — quick internal note:

- We've identified one serving group where an edge-case memory leak (observed under a specific KV-cache pattern + long prompt lengths) caused node OOMs and subsequent request retries, which cascaded into higher queuing and elevated latencies for colocated pools.
- Roll restart completed at 08:05 PT; initial metrics show tail latency dropping, but we are keeping the fallback routing in place for an hour to observe for recurrence.
- Pausing any non-essential deploys to us-west until the postmortem is complete.

Next steps for infra:
1) Run targeted health-checks across all us-west serving pools.
2) Increase KV-cache eviction aggressiveness for models with long-sequence usage.
3) Prepare a mitigation patch to be hot-fixed to the runtime by EOD.

If Horizon needs logs or specific request ids, we can scrub and share them.

- Markus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Postmortem: Intermittent hosted inference degradation (US-West) — root cause and remediation

Hi Elena / James / Ops team,

Thank you again for your patience. I’m sharing the postmortem summary and the remediation plan. Full doc attached: postmortem-draft.pdf (drive link above). Key points below.

Summary of impact:
- Window: 2026-04-12 08:45–09:05 UTC.
- Customers affected: hosted text generation endpoints in us-west region; estimated 2.1% of calls experienced elevated latencies and ~1.8% 5xx responses. Horizon Health saw several failed batch jobs during the window (we received those request ids).

Root cause:
- A memory handling regression in the serving runtime triggered under a specific KV-cache usage pattern with long prompts, causing node-level OOMs and retry storms. The regression was introduced in a runtime optimization landed two weeks prior.

Remediation & timeline:
1) Immediate: rollback of the regression and hot-fix deployed (applied 2026-04-12 08:55 PT).
2) Near-term: increase KV-cache eviction aggressiveness and add circuit-breaker thresholds for high-queue growth (target: 2 weeks).
3) Mid-term: add defensive tests and longer-duration soak runs for the affected serving configuration (target: 6 weeks).
4) Compensation: we will evaluate SLA impact and, if eligible, process credits via Finance. Rachel will coordinate.

Action items assigned:
- Markus K. — ship defensive unit/integration tests and runtime revert confirmation (due 2026-04-19).
- Lauren B. — customer communication and credits liaison (due 2026-04-16).
- Stephanie N. — update runbooks and health-check dashboards (due 2026-04-20).

If you'd like a walkthrough of the postmortem with the engineering team, I have a 30-minute slot Wed 2026-04-14 09:00 PT (calendar: https://cal.redwood.ai/event/pm-review-20260414).

Apologies again for the disruption. We understand the impact to your workflows and are prioritizing fixes and safeguards.

Best regards,
Rachel Kim

Redwood Inference
